hero.headline: Port St. Lucie residents rescue autistic child from retention pond
hero.teaser: A group of Port St. Lucie residents pulled an autistic child from a retention pond on Saturday morning after spotting him wandering alone near the water.
hero.body:
A group of Port St. Lucie residents rescued an autistic child from a retention pond on Saturday morning after noticing him wandering alone near the water. The residents were on their way to grab coffee when they spotted the child and sensed something was wrong, according to the Port St. Lucie Police Department.

The group stopped to help and tried to guide the child to safety. When the child tried to enter the pond, the residents followed him into the water and pulled him to safety. The child was covered in fire ants when they reached him.

The residents immediately called 911 and stayed with the child until officers arrived. Body camera video from the Port St. Lucie Police Department shows deputies talking to the residents and wiping fire ants off the child. The Port St. Lucie Police Department advises residents to follow their instincts if they see someone who could be in danger.

cards.headline: Palm City woman arrested after 36 Border Collies found living in feces-covered home
cards.teaser: Martin County Sheriff's Office deputies arrested 62-year-old Paige O'Donnell Monday after executing a search warrant at her Palm City home at 1245 SW Alligator .
cards.body:
Martin County Sheriff's Office deputies arrested 62-year-old Paige O'Donnell Monday after executing a search warrant at her Palm City home at 1245 SW Alligator Street, where they found 36 Border Collies living in what Sheriff John Budensiek described as deplorable conditions. Deputies and animal services officers wore Tyvek protective clothing to remove the dogs from a home covered in feces, urine-soaked materials, boxes and debris. O'Donnell faces charges of felony animal cruelty and misdemeanor improper confinement.

Budensiek said the dogs, which should be white and black, were solid black from being covered in feces. The house deteriorated so badly that about a foot and a half of drywall was gone, furniture was destroyed, and food and water bowls were covered in feces. Some dogs were skittish and hiding inside the home, making removal difficult. Deputies said it was extremely hot and O'Donnell may not have had air conditioning.

O'Donnell previously operated as an AKC Border Collie breeder. Budensiek said the last time officials were allowed inside the home was in 2020, when animals were in acceptable condition. Between 2020 and 2022, O'Donnell reportedly underwent treatment for alcohol abuse and began blocking officials from accessing her home. The sheriff's office conducted days of surveillance and last week persuaded O'Donnell to surrender one dog, which appeared malnourished and provided probable cause for Monday's warrant.

All 36 dogs removed from the home will be taken to the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast. O'Donnell is expected to appear in court Tuesday and will face at least 40 charges, according to Budensiek. Neighbor Kelsey Weidenheimer said it was sad to see the dogs in rough shape but was happy they were finally getting out. The case comes weeks after another Palm City woman was arrested when more than 100 dogs and cats were found in her home.

cards.headline: Florida insurers now require roof replacements at 15 years for homeowners
cards.teaser: Insurance companies across Florida have shortened the acceptable age for asphalt and composition shingle roofs from 20 years to 15 years, placing homeowners on a tighter timeline f
cards.body:
Insurance companies across Florida have shortened the acceptable age for asphalt and composition shingle roofs from 20 years to 15 years, placing homeowners on a tighter timeline for costly replacements. Most companies now require roofs to be 15 years old or newer to qualify for the best rates, according to Robert Norberg of Arden Insurance in Lantana. The change affects thousands of Florida homeowners who carry asphalt shingle roofs, the most common roofing material in the state.

Insurers view asphalt shingles as vulnerable to Florida's intense sun and strong winds. Metal roofs receive more favorable treatment, with some companies accepting them up to 40 years old. Tile roofs also face less restrictive age limits than asphalt. The shift in standards means homeowners with roofs approaching 15 years face pressure to replace them or accept higher premiums and limited coverage options.

Melissa Burt DeVriese, president of Security First Insurance, said the age of a roof represents the biggest factor in determining homeowner insurance rates. She said replacing an old roof can save thousands of dollars annually in premiums. Vero Beach homeowner Kelly Hagen reported a premium of nearly $9,000 and said she cannot find better quotes because her roof turns 15 years old this month. Multiple insurance agents told her they cannot help her secure lower rates.

The tightened standards arrive as Florida officials point to improvements in the homeowners insurance market, including new companies entering the state and some rate declines. Homeowners in recent years have already paid thousands for roof replacements under pressure from insurance companies seeking to reduce risk exposure. The 15-year threshold now applies statewide, creating what industry observers describe as a countdown clock for property owners with asphalt shingle roofs who want to maintain affordable coverage and avoid being dropped or non-renewed by their carriers.

cards.headline: Vindman holds fundraising edge over Nixon in Florida Democratic Senate primary
cards.teaser: Retired Army Lt. Alex Vindman and state Rep. Angie Nixon present contrasting campaigns ahead of the Aug. 18 primary to challenge Republican Sen. Ashley Moody.
cards.body:
Retired Army Lt. Alex Vindman has raised roughly $14.5 million through June in the Democratic primary for U.S. Senate, outpacing both his primary opponent and Republican Sen. Ashley Moody. Vindman is highlighting his military service and presenting himself as a candidate who can reach voters beyond the Democratic base. He has focused his campaign on the November general election and the need to place a congressional check on President Donald Trump, saying a Democratic House and Senate are essential because Republicans in office have abandoned their responsibilities to check presidential power.

Vindman must first defeat state Rep. Angie Nixon, a Jacksonville Democrat whom he has declined to debate. Nixon is countering Vindman's national profile with her Florida roots, a more progressive platform, and a working-class message centered on wages and affordability. Her campaign's social media posts have highlighted car trouble and a flat tire as evidence she faces the same problems as the voters she hopes to represent. At the Florida Capitol, Nixon has built a reputation as an outspoken protester, using a bullhorn during the fight over Florida's congressional maps and later facing charges following a sit-in demonstration at the governor's office.

Moody faces three lower-profile candidates in the Republican primary, none expected to seriously threaten the appointed senator. The latest Decision Desk HQ polling average gives Moody a seven-point advantage over Vindman, 47% to 40%, placing the race within competitive territory. Florida's primary takes place Aug. 18. The November winner will complete the final two years of a term and must run again in 2028 for a full six-year term.

cards.headline: Man rescues woman trapped on railroad tracks in Hobe Sound seconds before train arrives
cards.teaser: Josiah Baur lifted a railroad crossing gate to free Debbie Spoelstra from the tracks at Bridge Road and Dixie Highway in Hobe Sound Friday evening. The two met again Sunday at the same crossing.
cards.body:
Josiah Baur, 23, lifted a railroad crossing gate Friday evening to free Debbie Spoelstra's car from the tracks at Bridge Road and Dixie Highway in Hobe Sound seconds before a freight train passed through the intersection. Spoelstra was turning onto Bridge Road from Dixie Highway when a railroad crossing arm came down on her car, leaving her trapped between the gates. The arm got stuck on her car antenna, preventing her from reversing.

Baur was on his way home to Port St. Lucie from work when he stopped at the crossing and saw Spoelstra trapped. He put his car in park and ran across the tracks to lift the gate. Spoelstra backed her car away from the tracks seconds before the train passed. Dash-cam video captured the rescue.

Spoelstra and Baur met again at the railroad crossing Sunday and hugged. Spoelstra said she was grateful to Baur and believes a total stranger helping another person is remarkable. Baur said he was fortunate that God put him where he was.

Spoelstra said she was not texting or distracted while driving and was simply taken off guard by the crossing arms lowering. Witnesses say the crossing arm malfunctioned during the incident, and Spoelstra reported the problem to Florida East Coast Railway.

cards.headline: Indian River County Superintendent highlights new bus routing system on first day of school
cards.teaser: Indian River County is rolling out an entirely new routing system this year along with a new tracking app called Chipmunk that allows parents to know when buses are about to pick up or drop off students.
cards.body:
All bus routes in Indian River County were covered Monday. Superintendent David Moore said the district has enough drivers and drivers on standby. All bus stops are in different locations this year as the district optimizes the way it uses technology to make sure routes are very efficient.

In Martin County, the school district cut three bus routes this year to save costs. All students arrived and the three routes that were reduced caused no issues or delays. In St. Lucie County, parents with children not yet routed on a bus or who have a safety concern are encouraged to reach out to the transportation department by phone or through the transportation website.

hero.headline: Mets, Tortugas split Saturday doubleheader as Zayas powers Game 1 win
hero.teaser: Julio Zayas hit a go-ahead three-run homer for the second straight day, lifting St. Lucie to a 3-1 win before Daytona answered with a 15-7 victory in Game 2.
hero.body:
The St. Lucie Mets and Daytona Tortugas split a Saturday doubleheader at Clover Park, with the Mets taking the opener 3-1 before Daytona answered with a 15-7 victory in Game 2.

The split left the seven-game series tied 3-3 heading into Sunday’s finale. It was also the second time the teams split a doubleheader during the series after each club won once during Wednesday’s twin bill.

## Zayas delivers another go-ahead home run

Julio Zayas provided the biggest swing for St. Lucie in Game 1, hitting a go-ahead three-run home run in the fourth inning to erase a 1-0 Daytona lead.

The homer came one night after Zayas hit a walk-off home run in the bottom of the ninth inning Friday. Saturday’s blast was his third home run of the series.

St. Lucie’s pitching staff made the lead hold up.

Starter Nate Hall worked the first 1 2/3 innings before Caden Wooster took over. Wooster allowed Daytona’s only run when Arnaldo Lantigua hit a solo home run in the third inning.

Ernesto Mercedes followed with two scoreless innings, allowing four hits while striking out three to earn the win.

Miguel Mijias recorded the final five outs for his fourth save of the season, including a perfect seventh inning to close the game.

The Mets held Daytona to 1-for-8 with runners in scoring position and stranded 10 Tortugas runners.

The performance continued a sharp turnaround for St. Lucie’s pitching staff. From the ninth inning of Thursday’s game through the end of Saturday’s opener, the Mets allowed only one run after Daytona had scored 17 runs over the first eight innings Thursday.

Daytona starter Dusty Revis was charged with the loss despite throwing a six-inning complete game on just 63 pitches. Revis allowed five hits and three earned runs while becoming the first Tortugas pitcher since 2019 to record a complete game.

Elian Peña went 1-for-3 for St. Lucie and extended his hitting streak to 10 games.

## Daytona pulls away in Game 2

The nightcap was a much different game, with Daytona breaking a 6-6 tie during a decisive fifth inning.

Mets newcomer Wilmer Lugo appeared to escape the inning by striking out Henry Hunter looking on a 3-2 pitch. Hunter challenged the call using the ABS system, however, and the ruling was overturned to ball four, loading the bases.

Lugo then walked the next two hitters to force home a pair of runs. After Luis Sotillo entered in relief, a wild pitch allowed Hunter to score and stretched Daytona’s lead to 9-6.

Hunter delivered another major blow in the seventh inning, hitting a grand slam off Sotillo to push the Tortugas ahead 13-6.

For the second time in four games, the Mets eventually turned to Zayas to finish the game on the mound as a position player. He recorded the final four outs, allowing a two-run homer to Drew Davies with two outs in the seventh but no additional damage.

Logan Tanner earned the win for Daytona after throwing two scoreless innings of relief.

St. Lucie still produced several offensive highlights in the loss.

Simon Juan went 2-for-3 with a double and his ninth home run of the season.

Kuhio Aloy, the Mets’ 11th-round draft pick, hit a two-run homer in the third inning to tie the game at 6-6. It was Aloy’s first professional home run.

Lugo took the loss after being charged with three runs on one hit and four walks over 2/3 of an inning.

## Series finale set for Sunday

The Mets fell to 16-24 in the second half and 49-57 overall, while Daytona improved to 25-14 in the second half and 46-60 overall.

St. Lucie and Daytona will decide the series Sunday at Clover Park, with first pitch scheduled for 12:10 p.m.

Sunday is Little League Day. Little leaguers who attend wearing their team jerseys will receive free admission courtesy of Holiday Inn Express.

Her campaign's social media posts have highlighted car trouble and a flat tire as evidence she faces the same problems as the voters she hopes to represent. At the Florida Capitol, Nixon has built a reputation as an outspoken protester, using a bullhorn during the fight over Florida's congressional maps and later facing charges following a sit-in demonstration at the governor's office.

Moody faces three lower-profile candidates in the Republican primary, none expected to seriously threaten the appointed senator. The latest Decision Desk HQ polling average gives Moody a seven-point advantage over Vindman, 47% to 40%, placing the race within competitive territory. Florida's primary takes place Aug. 18. The November winner will complete the final two years of a term and must run again in 2028 for a full six-year term.

hero.headline: Man rescues woman trapped on railroad tracks in Hobe Sound seconds before train arrives
hero.teaser: Josiah Baur lifted a railroad crossing gate to free Debbie Spoelstra from the tracks at Bridge Road and Dixie Highway in Hobe Sound Friday evening. The two met again Sunday at the same crossing.
hero.body:
Josiah Baur, 23, lifted a railroad crossing gate Friday evening to free Debbie Spoelstra's car from the tracks at Bridge Road and Dixie Highway in Hobe Sound seconds before a freight train passed through the intersection. Spoelstra was turning onto Bridge Road from Dixie Highway when a railroad crossing arm came down on her car, leaving her trapped between the gates. The arm got stuck on her car antenna, preventing her from reversing.

Baur was on his way home to Port St. Lucie from work when he stopped at the crossing and saw Spoelstra trapped. He put his car in park and ran across the tracks to lift the gate. Spoelstra backed her car away from the tracks seconds before the train passed. Dash-cam video captured the rescue.

Spoelstra and Baur met again at the railroad crossing Sunday and hugged. Spoelstra said she was grateful to Baur and believes a total stranger helping another person is remarkable. Baur said he was fortunate that God put him where he was.

Spoelstra said she was not texting or distracted while driving and was simply taken off guard by the crossing arms lowering. Witnesses say the crossing arm malfunctioned during the incident, and Spoelstra reported the problem to Florida East Coast Railway.

cards.headline: Palm City woman arrested after 36 Border Collies found living in feces-covered home
cards.teaser: Martin County Sheriff's Office deputies arrested 62-year-old Paige O'Donnell Monday after executing a search warrant at her Palm City home at 1245 SW Alligator .
cards.body:
Martin County Sheriff's Office deputies arrested 62-year-old Paige O'Donnell Monday after executing a search warrant at her Palm City home at 1245 SW Alligator Street, where they found 36 Border Collies living in what Sheriff John Budensiek described as deplorable conditions. Deputies and animal services officers wore Tyvek protective clothing to remove the dogs from a home covered in feces, urine-soaked materials, boxes and debris. O'Donnell faces charges of felony animal cruelty and misdemeanor improper confinement.

Budensiek said the dogs, which should be white and black, were solid black from being covered in feces. The house deteriorated so badly that about a foot and a half of drywall was gone, furniture was destroyed, and food and water bowls were covered in feces. Some dogs were skittish and hiding inside the home, making removal difficult. Deputies said it was extremely hot and O'Donnell may not have had air conditioning.

O'Donnell previously operated as an AKC Border Collie breeder. Budensiek said the last time officials were allowed inside the home was in 2020, when animals were in acceptable condition. Between 2020 and 2022, O'Donnell reportedly underwent treatment for alcohol abuse and began blocking officials from accessing her home. The sheriff's office conducted days of surveillance and last week persuaded O'Donnell to surrender one dog, which appeared malnourished and provided probable cause for Monday's warrant.

All 36 dogs removed from the home will be taken to the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast. O'Donnell is expected to appear in court Tuesday and will face at least 40 charges, according to Budensiek. Neighbor Kelsey Weidenheimer said it was sad to see the dogs in rough shape but was happy they were finally getting out. The case comes weeks after another Palm City woman was arrested when more than 100 dogs and cats were found in her home.

cards.headline: Martin County schools begin year with on-time buses and new academic goals
cards.teaser: Superintendent Michael Maine said Monday that all buses arrived on time on the first day of school and the district is focused on eliminating C-rated schools and ensuring 100% of students are on reading level.
cards.body:
Superintendent Michael Maine greeted bus drivers at the transportation department Monday morning as Martin County schools began the year. District officials said enrollment this school year is flat and bus routes were consolidated to increase efficiency and save costs. Maine said all reports showed everything was on time and all students arrived, though there were some delays due to traffic.

Traffic appeared manageable outside Hobe Sound Elementary Monday morning, and one crossing guard said it was the best day since they started working there. Maine visited the now B-rated Hobe Sound Elementary, where third grade teacher Crystal Brandt said her class would write expectations together. A fourth grader said they were excited to have friends again.

Maine outlined the district's goals for the year: eliminating C-rated schools, ensuring 100% of students are on reading level, and making sure every student arrives home safely. Maine said he hopes by the end of the first week students feel safe and excited to be back and are starting to get back into the academic routine.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie residents rescue autistic child from retention pond
hero.teaser: A group of Port St. Lucie residents pulled an autistic child from a retention pond on Saturday morning after spotting him wandering alone near the water.
hero.body:
A group of Port St. Lucie residents rescued an autistic child from a retention pond on Saturday morning after noticing him wandering alone near the water. The residents were on their way to grab coffee when they spotted the child and sensed something was wrong, according to the Port St. Lucie Police Department.

The group stopped to help and tried to guide the child to safety. When the child tried to enter the pond, the residents followed him into the water and pulled him to safety. The child was covered in fire ants when they reached him.

The residents immediately called 911 and stayed with the child until officers arrived. Body camera video from the Port St. Lucie Police Department shows deputies talking to the residents and wiping fire ants off the child. The Port St. Lucie Police Department advises residents to follow their instincts if they see someone who could be in danger.

cards.headline: Mets, Tortugas split Saturday doubleheader as Zayas powers Game 1 win
cards.teaser: Julio Zayas hit a go-ahead three-run homer for the second straight day, lifting St. Lucie to a 3-1 win before Daytona answered with a 15-7 victory in Game 2.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets and Daytona Tortugas split a Saturday doubleheader at Clover Park, with the Mets taking the opener 3-1 before Daytona answered with a 15-7 victory in Game 2.

The split left the seven-game series tied 3-3 heading into Sunday’s finale. It was also the second time the teams split a doubleheader during the series after each club won once during Wednesday’s twin bill.

## Zayas delivers another go-ahead home run

Julio Zayas provided the biggest swing for St. Lucie in Game 1, hitting a go-ahead three-run home run in the fourth inning to erase a 1-0 Daytona lead.

The homer came one night after Zayas hit a walk-off home run in the bottom of the ninth inning Friday. Saturday’s blast was his third home run of the series.

St. Lucie’s pitching staff made the lead hold up.

Starter Nate Hall worked the first 1 2/3 innings before Caden Wooster took over. Wooster allowed Daytona’s only run when Arnaldo Lantigua hit a solo home run in the third inning.

Ernesto Mercedes followed with two scoreless innings, allowing four hits while striking out three to earn the win.

Miguel Mijias recorded the final five outs for his fourth save of the season, including a perfect seventh inning to close the game.

The Mets held Daytona to 1-for-8 with runners in scoring position and stranded 10 Tortugas runners.

The performance continued a sharp turnaround for St. Lucie’s pitching staff. From the ninth inning of Thursday’s game through the end of Saturday’s opener, the Mets allowed only one run after Daytona had scored 17 runs over the first eight innings Thursday.

Daytona starter Dusty Revis was charged with the loss despite throwing a six-inning complete game on just 63 pitches. Revis allowed five hits and three earned runs while becoming the first Tortugas pitcher since 2019 to record a complete game.

Elian Peña went 1-for-3 for St. Lucie and extended his hitting streak to 10 games.

## Daytona pulls away in Game 2

The nightcap was a much different game, with Daytona breaking a 6-6 tie during a decisive fifth inning.

Mets newcomer Wilmer Lugo appeared to escape the inning by striking out Henry Hunter looking on a 3-2 pitch. Hunter challenged the call using the ABS system, however, and the ruling was overturned to ball four, loading the bases.

Lugo then walked the next two hitters to force home a pair of runs. After Luis Sotillo entered in relief, a wild pitch allowed Hunter to score and stretched Daytona’s lead to 9-6.

Hunter delivered another major blow in the seventh inning, hitting a grand slam off Sotillo to push the Tortugas ahead 13-6.

For the second time in four games, the Mets eventually turned to Zayas to finish the game on the mound as a position player. He recorded the final four outs, allowing a two-run homer to Drew Davies with two outs in the seventh but no additional damage.

Logan Tanner earned the win for Daytona after throwing two scoreless innings of relief.

St. Lucie still produced several offensive highlights in the loss.

Simon Juan went 2-for-3 with a double and his ninth home run of the season.

Kuhio Aloy, the Mets’ 11th-round draft pick, hit a two-run homer in the third inning to tie the game at 6-6. It was Aloy’s first professional home run.

Lugo took the loss after being charged with three runs on one hit and four walks over 2/3 of an inning.

## Series finale set for Sunday

The Mets fell to 16-24 in the second half and 49-57 overall, while Daytona improved to 25-14 in the second half and 46-60 overall.

St. Lucie and Daytona will decide the series Sunday at Clover Park, with first pitch scheduled for 12:10 p.m.

Sunday is Little League Day. Little leaguers who attend wearing their team jerseys will receive free admission courtesy of Holiday Inn Express.
